steps.prompt: A line just touches a circle at one point. What angle does it make with the radius to that point? Try drawing a few.

cards.title: Tangent facts
cards.body: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point where it touches. The two tangents from an outside point are equal in length. So from $P$ at distance $d$ from the centre of a circle of radius $r$, each tangent has length $\sqrt{d^2 - r^2}$.

cards.title: Worked example: tangent length
cards.problem: Point $P$ is $13$ from the centre of a circle with radius $5$. How long is a tangent from $P$?

steps.text: The radius, the tangent and $OP$ make a right triangle with hypotenuse $13$: $13^2 - 5^2 = 144$.

cards.title: Equal tangents at work
cards.body: If a circle touches all four sides of a quadrilateral, $AB + CD = BC + DA$. For two circles with radii $r_1$ and $r_2$ whose centres are $d$ apart, a common external tangent has length $\sqrt{d^2 - (r_1 - r_2)^2}$, and an internal one (crossing between them) $\sqrt{d^2 - (r_1 + r_2)^2}$.

cards.title: Worked example: two circles
cards.problem: Two circles have radii $3$ and $8$, and their centres are $13$ apart. How long is a common external tangent?

steps.text: Slide the tangent towards the centres: it becomes a leg of a right triangle whose other leg is the difference of the radii.

try.prompt: What is the difference of the radii?
How long is the external tangent?

cards.title: The common trap: where the right angle is
cards.body: The right angle is between the radius and the tangent, at the point of touching. It is not at $P$ or at the centre. External tangents use the DIFFERENCE of the radii; internal tangents use the SUM.
